references.text: Addresses the same theme of redeeming property by a close relative (goel), establishing the principle of the kinsman's right to redeem.
Describes the possibility for a person to redeem themselves if they acquire sufficient means, paralleling 'if his hand reaches it' in verse 49.
The immediate context describing the situation where an Israelite has sold himself to a foreigner, and the right of redemption.
Boaz is identified as a goel (redeemer) from Elimelech's family, illustrating the redeemer's role in practice.
Boaz accepts the role of goel and explains that there is a closer relative who has the first right to redeem.
The closer relative renounces his right of redemption, and Boaz takes over the role as goel - practical application of the redeemer principle.
Jeremiah exercises his right as goel by purchasing his cousin Hanamel's field in Anathoth.
Refers to the redeemer (goel) in connection with the guilt offering, and what happens if there is no redeemer.
Rules for redeeming things dedicated to the Lord, showing the broader principle of redemption.
